schema_cannot_express.note: access_tier assumes one access tier per app. These rows have more than one API product at different tiers, so no enum member is correct -- the question is malformed, not the answer. Excluded from both rates. No enum member was added: the gap is recorded, not patched.

agent_filled_pass_vs_human.finding: The agent-filled pass disagreed with the human on 2 of 4 rows the pipeline called self-serve. It called them misses; the vendor's pages say the pipeline was right. This is direct evidence that a second model reading the same class of page is not independent verification -- which is exactly the caveat this artifact carried on its own face before the human check existed. The caveat was correct.

corpus_projection.reason: only 3 scoreable rows, below the 5 needed to state a rate. Projecting a corpus-wide share from this sample would assert precisely the magnitude the sample cannot support. The direction of the error is established; its size is not.

why_this_test_and_not_the_cross_tab: Two explanations survive for a mostly self-serve corpus: the corpus really is mostly self-serve, or the extractor reads documented API as obtainable credentials. The tier x confidence cross-tab cannot separate them. A bias uniform across confidence cohorts produces a null result there BY CONSTRUCTION -- the cross-tab detects only a bias that concentrates in the weak cohort, so its null result is evidence about confidence, not about correctness. Ground truth from the vendor's own page is the only test that distinguishes them, and that is what this file scores.
sample_note: The sample is 3 scoreable rows, enriched with expected-gated products. It bounds the DIRECTION of the error, not its magnitude. Not a random sample and not a corpus-wide error rate: these are the rows most likely to be wrong, chosen for that reason. What it establishes is that the errors run one way -- gated products read as self-serve, never the reverse. What it cannot establish is how many rows in the corpus are affected.
verdict: DIRECTION ONLY. 3 scoreable self-serve rows is below the 5 needed to state a rate, so no magnitude is claimed here. What the sample does support is the direction: the miss (33% of 3) is a gated product read as self-serve, and 4 of 4 gated calls were correct. Errors run one way -- the method over-reports reachability and never under-reports it. The sample is also enriched with expected-gated products, so it bounds the direction of the error, not its magnitude.
